_metadata.description: Fixed evaluation framework for scientific-agent decisions. scientific_control.py gives these criteria to the planning agent, materializes its narrow decision into run_plan.json, and validate_run_plan.py blocks structurally incomplete plans before simulation.
_metadata.see_also: polymer_rules.json:electrostatics_decision_guide is the prototype for this structure (D-03 policy).

evidence_levels.high: Class-specific MD validation paper reproduces a target property (density or Tg) within ~10%, with DOI.
evidence_levels.medium: Force field validated for a related class or by builder constraint; no class-specific MD Tg/density paper yet.
evidence_levels.low: No validation; choice made by analogy or builder availability only. Reasoned planning REQUIRED.

confidence_gate.description: Planning context is keyed per exact canonical SMILES, never merely by class. A validated protocol is evidence the scientific agent may select; it does not bypass the planning-agent call. polymer_rules.json remains a starting-hypothesis scaffold, not a trust signal.
confidence_gate.gate_direction: The plan_mode↔system-validation gate is ASYMMETRIC. Only `deterministic` for a SMILES that is not `protocol_validated` (or whose validated_properties don't cover this run's requested properties) is a bypass that the Critic must ESCALATE. `reasoned` for an already-validated SMILES is the SAFE direction — never escalate it; it subjects every decision to full step-3 enforcement instead of fast-path auto-approve. A budget-forced deviation to a non-default ladder for an otherwise-validated SMILES (e.g. a rate ladder infeasible in a tight wall-clock budget) is exactly what reasoned mode exists for.

validated.behavior: The scientific planning agent still runs, sees the exact-SMILES characterization record, and normally selects the validated protocol without overrides. Code materializes and validates the plan; deterministic stage scripts execute it. emc_seed/velocity_seed remain runtime values and are logged after submission.
validated.rationale: This exact molecule's protocol is validated; reproducibility outranks re-derivation. Do not re-reason a settled, cited decision.

novel_or_partially_validated.behavior: The scientific planning agent reasons each decision against the policy below, records evidence/confidence/alternatives, and names the dominant uncertainty. validate_run_plan.py blocks missing criteria or evidence before deterministic execution.
novel_or_partially_validated.applies_to: canonical_smiles absent from system_characterization_cache.json, protocol_validated=false, or validated_properties does not cover the requested properties. Cached measured timing values may still be reused as evidence and bounded overrides.

require: mpi>=4 for any PPPM/charged class2 system ON THE GPU PACKAGE (engine=gpu): mpi=1 starves kspace ~75x there — never launch it. This does NOT apply to engine=kokkos, where kspace is GPU-resident and mpi=1 IS the correct PCFF/OPLS default (by_forcefield.pcff). Only flag mpi=1 when engine=gpu.

UA classes (TraPPE: PHYC/PDIE) route to GPU package with `neigh yes`, mpi=1, 1 GPU/run (neighbor build is ~71% of the loop and offloads to the GPU; script_generator emits `neigh yes` automatically for use_trappe). This is 3.7x vs CPU mpi=4 and beats KOKKOS on small UA cells (run-0 parity PASS 2026-06-20). NOT pair-only GPU (neigh on CPU ties CPU) and NOT CPU mpi=4 (the old default). PSTR (Polystyrenics) is PCFF, not TraPPE-UA — do not include it here.
small (<10k-atom) cells use 1 GPU per run, not 4 (comm overhead, GPU underfill)
Sum of mpi across concurrent runs <= 18 physical cores (one GPU-heavy run per GPU)
a multi-GPU pin (gpu_per_run>=2) requires BOTH an estimated cell >~10k atoms AND benchmark support (directional_probe.recommended_by_ff[fam].gpu>=2 on a matching host); otherwise use 1 GPU

when hardware_policy.values_are_benchmarked=false OR the live host (nvidia-smi) does not match directional_probe.measured_on (the field that records where the probe ran — NOT the stale top-level hardware_policy.host, and NOT directional_probe.host which is null and would always mismatch), any non-default D-08 pin MUST be accompanied by a planned hardware_benchmark probe and confidence:low — else keep the by_forcefield default
prefer: when values_are_benchmarked=true AND directional_probe.measured_on matches the live host (nvidia-smi) AND the estimated cell is within ~[0.5x, 2x] of directional_probe.recommended_by_ff[fam].cell_atoms: adopt recommended_by_ff[fam] (engine/gpu/mpi) over the by_forcefield default — this is how measured optima reach runs

otherwise treat directional_probe ABSOLUTE ns/day as a HINT only — but a RATIO measured under uniform contention (all arms niced on the same busy box) plus a run-0 parity PASS is sufficient to flip an engine default, as was done for TraPPE neigh-yes (3.7x ratio, 0.000% parity, 2026-06-20). Do NOT bake in an absolute throughput claim from a contended sweep, and keep values_are_benchmarked=false until a drained-box sweep exists.
hardware.rationale: Hardware config is a function of FF cost structure (UA lj/cut vs PCFF class2+pppm) AND cell size (the GPU-saturation / PPPM all-to-all crossover), so it belongs in policy, not ad-hoc submit-time choice. The live anti-patterns: mpi=1 PCFF on the GPU-package (~2.4 ns/day, ~75x slow — but mpi=1 IS correct for PCFF/OPLS on KOKKOS, where kspace is on the GPU); and UA on the GPU with neigh on the CPU (pair-only offload ties CPU). UA on the GPU with `neigh yes` is the CORRECT default (3.7x), NOT an anti-pattern. A D-08_hardware deviation flows through decided_params (engine/gpu_per_run/mpi_ranks) into stage_params.apply_plan. The conservative gate above keeps the default until a CLEAN (values_are_benchmarked=true), host-matched, in-size benchmark exists.
hardware.tooling: orchestration/scripts/select_hardware.py implements this policy's require/prefer clauses (FF-alias resolution, cell-atom estimate, threshold comparison, deviate-from-default diff, staleness flagging) mechanically. The Planner calls it and transcribes its D-08 decision row + any decided_params override + uncertainties entry verbatim — it does NOT re-derive these thresholds in prose, so this policy stays the single source of truth for the numbers.

require: the chosen FF must have parameter coverage for every atom type in the SMILES
force field assigned AFTER polymerization for RadonPy path (never before; cross-stage rule 0)
forcefield.rationale: FF choice dominates property accuracy. A choice without literature_support + validation_data is low-confidence and the Critic must flag it. Alternatives with their known error must be recorded (e.g. GAFF2_mod Tg error >45% for PMMA).
forcefield.tooling: orchestration/scripts/select_forcefield.py implements this policy's require clauses mechanically: ff_capability.py builds the SMILES under each field as a HARD admissibility gate (parameter coverage is measured, never read off a table), ff_provenance.py flags parameters that were locally patched, silently zeroed, or taken from a wildcard fallback, and ff_domain.py's archive prior is REPORTED ONLY. The Planner calls it and transcribes its D-01 decision row, decided_params override and uncertainties entry verbatim.
forcefield.evidence_source: orchestration/scripts/ff_capability.py (admissibility, measured per SMILES); orchestration/scripts/ff_provenance.py + emc_fields/manifest.json (parameter provenance); polymer_rules.json:classes.<CLASS>.{preferred_ff,ff_justification_doi,ff_note}
forcefield.archive_prior_is_not_a_ranking: ff_domain.py's leave-one-family-out backtest on this archive measures corr(extrapolated atom fraction, |density error|) = -0.64 and |K error| = -0.26 — both NEGATIVE, i.e. more extrapolation went with better agreement. The signal is confounded and must never gate or rank a field; it records what an archive-carried accuracy prior is worth, nothing more.
forcefield.provenance_flag_is_acknowledgeable: A blocking provenance flag does not veto a field — several classes have exactly one route (PSIL builds only because of a local OPLS patch). It is cleared by an uncertainties entry naming the flagged field, so the plan carries the parameter's origin as a stated uncertainty instead of inheriting it silently.

require: charge method consistent with the chosen FF (e.g. TraPPE-UA embeds charges; PCFF uses bond-increment/Gasteiger)
charges.rationale: Apolar UA backbones embed charges in the FF (no QM). Polar all-atom systems need explicit charges. Solubility/CED accuracy degrades for Gasteiger-charged apolar systems — flag charge_method downstream.

require: heteroatom-containing or |q|>0.1e backbones MUST use pppm; pure C/H backbones MAY use lj_cut
electrostatics.rationale: Already encoded as polymer_rules.json:electrostatics_decision_guide. This policy points the Critic at that guide; neglecting long-range Coulomb biases density/Tg by 5-20% for polar polymers.

require: DP above the Fox-Flory plateau (DP>=20) for Tg targets
bulk_modulus targets need DP/nchain above the entanglement-MW threshold (per-class)

cell large enough to avoid self-imaging — MECHANIZED as spatial.finite_size by check_equilibration_comprehensive (needs cutoff_A, threaded from polymer_rules.json via stage_params.py). Two binding Class A criteria on L = min(Lx,Ly,Lz): L >= 2*cutoff_A (minimum image; below it an atom interacts with its own periodic image and the pair potential itself is wrong) and L >= 2*Rg (each chain overlaps its own image, biasing packing and therefore density and the moduli). L >= R_ee is reported but ADVISORY — running slightly below it is common in published polymer MD and far weaker evidence than the 2*Rg criterion. Both binding failures are STRUCTURAL: no trajectory length fixes a box dimension, so the remedy is to raise nchain and rebuild (L grows as nchain^(1/3) at fixed density)
system_size.rationale_finite_size: This clause existed as prose from the start and nothing checked it. Measuring the 36-run archive: minimum image is satisfied everywhere (L/2*cutoff 1.49-2.44, 0 violations), but FOUR runs violate chain self-imaging — PEEK1 at L/2Rg=0.74, PSU4 0.78, PSU2 0.99, PE2 0.96 — and seven have L < R_ee. The two worst sit in exactly the families with independently documented density anomalies (PEEK ~5% under-dense, PSU -4% systematic), and PEEK1 also carries the degenerate 0.0 K transition width. Several independent signals therefore converge on those cells simply being too small for their chains — a physical explanation for anomalies previously attributed to force-field bias. Supersedes the INCONCLUSIVE_SIZE homogeneity guard, which could only fire below ~300 atoms (the adaptive voxel grid pins atoms/voxel near 25 by construction) and so never fired on a real cell.
system_size.rationale: Too-small DP biases Tg low and K high. Too-large wastes GPU budget. The probe option (fast small-cell density screen, ROADMAP E3) reduces finite-size uncertainty cheaply before committing the full cell.
system_size.tooling: orchestration/scripts/select_system_size.py implements this policy's Fox-Flory and entanglement-MW require clauses mechanically: the DP floor is a function of properties_requested (Fox-Flory for tg, entanglement DP@Me for bulk_modulus, no floor for density-only), entanglement Me is resolved per-member via run_name (never generalized across a multi-member class), and a class default already above its floor is reported as size_over_provisioned rather than silently shrunk. The Planner calls it and transcribes its D-04 decision row + any decided_params override + uncertainties entry verbatim — it does NOT re-derive these thresholds in prose. The L>=2*Rg finite-size half of this policy's require clause remains separately mechanized by check_equilibration_comprehensive/validate_run_plan.py's _finite_size_findings, not this script.

require: check_equilibration_comprehensive overall_pass=True before ANY property extraction (cross-stage rule 2); EXCEPT glassy systems with DP>=30 OR ct_gate_reliable=false, which use require_glassy (see below); EXCEPT rubbery systems (T_workflow_K > Tg_K), which use require_rubbery (see below)
require_glassy: for regime=glassy AND (DP>=30 OR class ct_gate_reliable=false): gate on density plateau within experimental range AND Poisson-corrected density homogeneity signal CV<=0.11 AND P2 nematic<0.10 AND energy drift/SEM within bounds AND n_eff_density>=20. The melt chain-self-diffusion metrics (C(t) decay, MSD diffusivity, MSID slope, Rg chain-chain CV) are ADVISORY (logged, non-blocking). overall_pass may be False on these advisory metrics without blocking property extraction. CRITICAL: 'density plateau within experimental range' is a BINDING gate, not a soft warning — convergence (drift/SEM) is necessary but NOT sufficient, because a kinetically trapped (under-annealed) glass converges perfectly at a too-low density. If the 300 K density is below experiment-band (see density_value_binding), the verdict CANNOT be PASS-with-caveats on a bare 'known force-field bias' assertion — route through density_value_binding first.
require_rubbery: for regime=rubbery (T_workflow_K > Tg_K, e.g. PE/PP/PIB/PBD/PI at 300K): gate on density block-SEM < 1% AND Poisson-corrected density homogeneity signal CV <= 0.11 AND energy drift/SEM within bounds AND n_eff_density >= 20. The terminal chain-reptation metrics (C(t) full decay, MSD diffusivity, tau_relax, MSID slope, Rg chain-chain CV) are ADVISORY (logged, non-blocking). overall_pass may be False on these reptation-limited metrics without blocking property extraction, provided the density/energy gating criteria pass.
density_value_binding: When the production density at 300 K falls below experiment by more than 5% (glassy) — i.e. outside the pass band, including the former soft -5..-10% 'warning' zone — you MUST run tool:assess_cooling_contraction(melt_data=npt_production_out.data, glass_data=npt_prod300_out.data, exp_density_gcm3, tg_K, t_equil_K) BEFORE accepting the cell, and route on its verdict:

- UNDER_ANNEALED_COOLING (melt density OK, cell under-contracted on cooling): the deficit is frozen-in free volume. Recover via re_melt_slow_recool (see equilibration recovery). Do NOT EXTEND at 300 K (a glass cannot densify below Tg) and do NOT accept as force-field bias.

- MELT_STAGE_DEFICIT (melt density already low) or rubbery: the deficit is at the equilibrium/melt stage — force-field underbinding OR melt-stage under-annealing, not separable a priori. The melt_hold remedy now escalates the cheaper, more-targeted lever first (attempt 1 doubles eq_annealing_cycles to give the cell another chance to escape a bad initial pack) before falling back to a bounded isothermal melt-anneal hold (attempt 2, melt_hold_ns=5 -- deliberately far short of the ~100 ns NkepsuMbitou2025 cites for full convergence: PolyJarvis is a quick-survey tool, not a per-polymer optimizer, so this rung is a bounded diagnostic probe and a deficit that survives both rungs escalates to human review rather than buying more wall-clock). Acceptance as 'force-field bias' is permitted ONLY with the assess_cooling_contraction evidence recorded in D-05 (melt gap + contraction shortfall), flagged unresolved, and ideally after both rungs have been tried. A bare 'known PCFF bias' caveat is NOT sufficient justification.

- extrapolation_reliable=False (cooling span >300 K, e.g. PEEK): the melt/cooling split is indicative only; lean on the absolute glass-vs-exp density and prefer re_melt_slow_recool before any FF-bias acceptance.

Rationale: convergence (drift/SEM flat) proves the cell stopped moving, not that it stopped at the right density. This routing replaces the soft warning band that let PMMA (-6%, under-annealed cooling) be accepted four times as 'PCFF bias' (2026-06; the 'PCFF PMMA within 2%' claim was itself a Tang2022 misattribution — the real source NkepsuMbitou2025 reaches 1.19 via ~100 ns of melt annealing).
equilibration.rationale: This is the philosophy's 'convince me it is equilibrated' gate — already implemented as check_equilibration_comprehensive. The policy makes it a hard plan success_criterion, not an afterthought. The Validator enforces it after the equil stage.
equilibration.rationale_glassy: For glassy high-MW polymers (DP>=30), and for rigid-aromatic classes with ct_gate_reliable=false (PSFO/PKTN at any DP — C(t) is structurally undefined via atom-type backbone), melt chain self-diffusion is unattainable on MD timescales (measured tau_relax ~3.6e9 ps for DP=60 PVC; a 1-2 ns extend moves C(t) only ~0.4%->0.5%), so overall_pass=True is unsatisfiable by construction. The 5-cycle high-T anneal substitutes for melt self-diffusion. The metrics that actually bound structural quality for density/Tg/glassy-K_T — density plateau, homogeneity CV, P2 — are gating; the diffusion-limited metrics are advisory. Authorized 2026-06-20 (PVC1 route-back, user-approved). Applies campaign-wide to glassy revision polymers.
equilibration.rationale_rubbery: For rubbery high-MW polymers at T_workflow_K > Tg_K, terminal chain reptation time >> accessible MD simulation time even at high melt temperature (measured tau_relax ~88 ns KWW for DP-120 PE at 550 K; MSD alpha=0.28 subdiffusive). The requested properties — density (packing/cohesion), Tg (segmental kinetics), rubbery-K (P-V EOS volumetric response) — are governed by local packing and cohesive energy, not terminal reptation; each property has its own downstream gate (density block-SEM, Tg bilinear R^2, Murnaghan volume convergence per pressure point). Authorized 2026-06-22 (user-approved, PE1 critic round-2 precedent). Applies campaign-wide to PHYC/PDIE rubbery replicates.
equilibration.eq_annealing_cycles_is_a_real_runtime_kn: Superseded 2026-08-16 (commit a21a426): eq_annealing_cycles is a real runtime knob, consumed by generate_equilibration_workflow, which materializes anneal_NN_heat/anneal_NN_cool NVT cycle pairs before nvt_softheat — the chain runs N cycles, not one. It IS prescribable: the melt_hold remedy (workflow_engine.py) escalates it as the first rung on a MELT_STAGE_DEFICIT finding, before falling back to a heavy isothermal melt hold. See density_value_binding below for the current MELT_STAGE_DEFICIT routing — not restated here to avoid a second copy drifting independently.

gate_classes.purpose: A gate rejects physically/thermodynamically inadmissible results; predicting agreement with experiment is a separate job needing separate evidence. Classify a check before arguing about whether to bind it.
gate_classes.A_admissibility: Binds on physical or thermodynamic impossibility. Justified by the physics it violates, NOT by how often it fires — a validity gate that never fires on the archive is still correct, because its value is what it rejects in future. Never fixable by EXTEND, never excused as known force-field bias. Members: p2 (amorphousness), density_homogeneity, finite_size (minimum image and chain self-imaging), plus the mechanical/thermal admissibility sets under property_method and tg_protocol.
gate_classes.B_convergence: Binds on insufficient sampling of an otherwise valid state; judged by statistical adequacy. Remedy is EXTEND. Members: density/energy drift and block-SEM, n_eff_density.
gate_classes.C_agreement: Binds on distance from experiment; the ONLY class where correlation with known-good reference values is the right evidence. Members: density_in_band, routed via density_value_binding.
gate_classes.D_advisory: Timescale-limited quantities unattainable within accessible MD, so binding them makes the gate unsatisfiable by construction. Logged, never blocking. Members: ct, msd_not_trapped, msid_gaussian, rg; plus residual_stress until its magnitude bound is calibrated.
gate_classes.verdict_vocabulary: Subsystem-prefixed so a bare token in a run_log, RECOVERY block or summary row names the field that produced it. equil_verdict: PASS | EXTEND | STRUCTURAL_FAIL | FAIL (unprefixed, Foundation-only, unambiguous). tg_gate_verdict: TG_REPORTABLE | TG_REVIEW | TG_NOT_REPORTABLE. bm_gate_verdict: BM_REPORTABLE | BM_FALLBACK_DEFORM | BM_INADMISSIBLE. deform_gate_verdict: DEFORM_REPORTABLE | DEFORM_INADMISSIBLE. density_homogeneity.verdict: HOMOG_PASS | HOMOG_HETEROGENEOUS. finite_size.verdict: SIZE_PASS | SIZE_CHAIN_SELF_IMAGE | SIZE_MIN_IMAGE_VIOLATION.
gate_classes.never_bind_a_z_score: A significance threshold grows as sqrt(n), so it gets HARDER to pass the longer a cell is equilibrated — the same defect as binding C(t). Bind magnitudes against a physical scale and read z only as resolved/unresolved.

equilibration.rationale_homogeneity_signal_cv: The raw voxel CV mixes real heterogeneity with counting shot noise, and the noise floor moves with cell size: integer rounding of the adaptive grid (target ~25 atoms/voxel) leaves 20.5-32.8 atoms/voxel across the 36-run archive, so poisson_cv spans 0.175-0.221 and a fixed raw-CV bound of 0.25 implies an effective signal threshold varying 0.117-0.179 — a 1.5x swing in strictness driven by cell size alone. It mis-ranked 15 ordered pairs (PS3 signal CV 0.168 PASSED while PSU3 at 0.124 FAILED). Gating the noise-subtracted signal CV makes the criterion mean the same thing at every cell size. Threshold 0.11 is calibrated on the archive: the three families with independently confirmed heterogeneous underpacking (PMMA -6%, PS aromatic-PCFF underpack, PSU -4%) span 0.120-0.192 while every other family spans 0.000-0.094 — a clean gap with perfect family-level separation. PEEK lands on the pass side at 0.021-0.072, correctly: its ~5% under-density is uniform force-field underbinding, not spatial heterogeneity, and the two need different remedies. The new rule is a strict superset of the old — nothing that failed now passes.
equilibration.rationale_n_eff_density: n_eff = n_production/tau_eff, with tau_eff the integrated statistical inefficiency. Two bugs previously made this unusable: compute_tau_eff averaged the blocking curve's TAIL (largest block sizes, 4-8 blocks) instead of its plateau, underestimating tau by 4.3-38.9x, and n_eff carried a spurious extra factor of 2 on top of an already-integrated tau. Fixed, the archive spans n_eff 11-899 and only PMMA1 (11) and PEEK4 (17) fall below 20. Class B, so it routes EXTEND — more NPT at the same temperature is exactly the remedy. Do not raise to 30-50: that fires on runs whose density is demonstrably converged.
equilibration.rationale_residual_stress: Under fix npt iso only the pressure TRACE is controlled, so the box is cubic by construction and box-shape isotropy is a vacuous check (measured spread exactly 0.00%). A persistent difference among Pxx/Pyy/Pzz is NOT vacuous: it is a departure from mechanical equilibrium, and the Murnaghan EOS assumes a hydrostatic reference state. Measured: melts are stress-isotropic (z=0.06-3.1) while glassy cells carry 100-290 atm of resolved deviatoric stress (z=3.8-12.3), i.e. 10-29% of the +/-1000 atm pressure increment — frozen in during cooling, though sign flips implicate anneal-cycle count more than cooling rate. It does not correlate with K (within-family Spearman 0.090, p=0.674), which is the expected and irrelevant result for a Class A condition on an archive with no admissible comparison group. Emitted and logged now; bind the MAGNITUDE as a fraction of bm_pressures_atm once calibrated, never the z-score.
equilibration.rationale_density_value_binding: A converged glassy density that is too low is the signature of kinetic trapping (under-annealing during cooling), NOT automatically force-field bias. The two need different remedies — re-melt+slow-recool vs heavy-melt-anneal — and only assess_cooling_contraction (melt-vs-glass density decomposition) can tell them apart. Before this gate, the equil-checker validated CONVERGENCE only; PMMA/PS/PEEK underdensities were accepted as 'PCFF bias' without testing it. Authorized 2026-06-29 (PMMA forensic: melt 1.055 matches exp, cooled only +5.8% vs +12% expected -> trapped).

remedy_economics.purpose: Decide whether a recovery rung is worth spending BEFORE spending it. A rung buys accuracy with wall time, which only works when the residual is a sampling term. Classify the residual first, then price the lever.
remedy_economics.tooling: orchestration/scripts/remedy_economics.py implements this policy mechanically (residual classification, log-linear closure forecast, break-even lever, margin factor, cost to the physical target). recover.md's ladder calls it and the recovery-agent transcribes its verdict + reason verbatim - neither re-derives these thresholds in prose, so this policy stays the single source of truth for the numbers.
remedy_economics.applies_to: Every ladder rung that trades wall time for a property value: RE-ANNEAL multipliers, HEAVY-MELT-ANNEAL MULT, EXTEND beyond the first, and any proposal to re-run a Tg sweep at a slower rate. NOT to REBUILD-LARGER (see class_A_is_always_worth_paying).
remedy_economics.test_1_residual_type: gap_over_sem = |target_floor - current| / SEM. At or below 3*SEM the residual is VARIANCE and more sampling is the right lever. Above it the residual is BIAS and wall time cannot reduce it - no rung length changes a biased estimator's expectation. A Class B gate whose gap is bias has been mis-classified; re-classify before extending.
remedy_economics.test_2_closure: Fit metric = A + B*ln(lever) over the rungs already spent, solve for the break-even lever at target_floor, and take margin_factor as break_even/delivered (or its inverse when a larger lever is the improvement). Below 1.0 the rung is forecast to fail outright. Below min_margin_factor it is a bet the forecast cannot call, and the rung is not worth its wall time. A single spent rung determines no slope: spend exactly one to measure it, then re-run this check before spending a second.
remedy_economics.test_3_converged_or_lever_dependent: Extrapolate to the PHYSICAL target (the experimental value, never the band edge) and price it at the last rung's measured wall time. Above converged_cost_ceiling_hours the property is lever-limited: a rung that buys a passing but lever-dependent number is worse than an annotated failing one, because the annotation is what survives into the manuscript. STOP and annotate even when test 2 passes.
remedy_economics.class_A_is_always_worth_paying: Class A admissibility failures are bias that the class's own structural remedy removes COMPLETELY and at a bounded one-time cost - rebuild the cell, re-route the method. They are the one case where spending is unconditionally correct, and the economics tests do not apply. PEEK1 at L/2Rg=0.822 paid a full Phase A restart and got the whole term removed; that is the trade this policy exists to distinguish from PMMA1's.
remedy_economics.rationale: Every residual in the 2026-08-11 runs was bias, not variance: PMMA1 density SEM 0.0003 g/cm3 against a 0.064 gap to 1.19 (~210x), cis-PBD1 Tg fit uncertainty 8.9 K against a 45.2 K method gap and a 34-57 K rate offset, PEEK1 L/2Rg=0.822 which no trajectory length fixes. Each stopping call was correct and each was made by a human at the point the mechanized ladder said 'spend the next rung'. The ladder prices nothing: it escalates 2x then 4x regardless of whether the forecast clears. On PMMA1 the recovery-agent had already done this arithmetic by hand (break-even 83.6 K/ns, 4x delivering 62.5, ~1.3x margin, and a physical target ~2 orders of magnitude out of reach) and still had to route the decision to a human because no policy licensed it to stop. This block licenses it.
remedy_economics.rationale_min_margin_factor: 2.0 is a judgement calibrated on one case, not a derived constant, and is the clause to revisit first as evidence accumulates. PMMA1's rung-2 forecast carried 1.33x and the human stopped; the archive contains no spent rung with a recorded forecast on the other side of the line. Note that a two-point history has zero residual degrees of freedom, so the fit reports no prediction band - margin_factor deliberately measures headroom in the LEVER rather than dressing a two-point extrapolation in a standard error it cannot support.
remedy_economics.rationale_converged_cost_ceiling_hours: 200 h is invented, not derived - the same honesty that applies to min_margin_factor, and it fires the more consequential verdict of the two (a rung that would clear the gate is refused because the value behind it would still be lever-dependent). It is set at roughly one campaign's worth of GPU time on this workstation, so 'reaching the true value costs more than the whole campaign' is the thing it detects. The verdicts it has to separate are not close to it: PMMA1's physical target prices at 2503 h and every SPEND case at well under 50 h, so nothing in the archive lands near the boundary and no evidence yet constrains it further. Revisit it only when a run does land near it.
remedy_economics.rationale_not_an_empirical_prior: These tests rest on physics arithmetic, never on historical rung hit-rates. PEEK1's gate code was fixed by a concurrent session between its EXTEND and PASS verdicts, so that PASS is not evidence the extension was necessary - the archive cannot support a 'does EXTEND usually work' prior, and this policy does not ask it to.

require: never report Tg without verifying bilinear fit R^2 (cross-stage rule 3)

reportability is mechanized as extract_thermal's tg_gate_verdict — route on it, never re-derive it: NOT_REPORTABLE (fit_quality=POOR or primary_fit_invalid) blocks reporting the Tg; REVIEW (|Tg_K - Tg_alternative_K| > 20 K) halts to human review first. Class A admissibility conditions already enforced inside that rating: transition_width_c_K < 5 K (a zero-width glass transition is impossible — a sharp-kink fit artifact that can still score r^2 > 0.997, as PMMA1 did at 0.1 K width and EXCELLENT), slope_signs_valid (both dR/dT < 0), slope_ordering_valid (alpha_rubbery > alpha_glassy), and tg_pinned_to_sweep_endpoint. Blocking the REPORT is separate from the is_glassy ROUTING, which may still fall back to the plan's experimental_tg_K
T sweep range must bracket experimental_tg_K with margin

default single-rate-primary sweeps at the HIGHEST configured tg_rates_K_per_ns entry, so that entry especially must clear tg_min_steps_per_T: N=tg_t_step_K/(rate*dt_fs*1e-6) >= floor (default 200000 steps=200ps@dt=1fs; TraPPE-UA dt=2fs floor=100000). Critic MUST recompute N independently — never trust the decision's prose arithmetic. Retired [40,160,400] gave 50/125ps degenerate fits (cis-PBD2, PEEK2)

classes whose highest configured rate is documented as unreliable (PKTN, PSFO — cold-start/degenerate fit on the rigid-aromatic staircase) must carry tg_slope_gate_fallback="slowest_rate" in polymer_rules/decided_params so the thermal track runs tg_rates_K_per_ns[0] instead of the highest-rate default; the critic verifies this is set for any class with known highest-rate degeneracy, not transcribed blindly.
tg_protocol.rationale_tg_method_gap_exemption: The primary/alternative Tg gap exceeds 20 K on 4 of the 8 archived Tg runs (PEEK1 32.7, PSU1 40.3, cis-PBD1 41.6, cis-PBD2 80.1) — half the thermal track, concentrated in the rigid-aromatic classes whose highest-rate staircase degeneracy is already documented. Binding it without the tg_slope_gate_fallback exemption would repeat the C(t) mistake: a gate that fires mostly where a known, already-handled artifact lives. Exempt classes record the gap as a reason without forcing REVIEW, so cis-PBD1 (PDIE, no documented degeneracy) still routes REVIEW while PSU1 does not.
tg_protocol.rationale_dcp_reported_not_gated: A glass transition with essentially no heat-capacity step is not a glass transition, so a dCp floor looks like a natural Class A gate. It is emitted (dCp_weak_step_flag) but NOT bound: the two lowest archived values, PEEK1 0.037 and cis-PBD2 0.018 J/g/K against a typical 0.1-0.3, are already caught by transition_width_degenerate and slope_sign_invalid respectively. A floor would add no independent discrimination while inventing a threshold the data cannot justify, and a weak-but-real transition can legitimately show a small step.
tg_protocol.rationale: A too-narrow T range gives R^2<0.80 / <4 bins (known /recover failure mode). Planning the range from experimental_tg_K +/- margin catches this before the sweep runs.

require: glassy bulk_modulus via Murnaghan NPT compression at 300 K (primary — symmetric, cell-size independent; Wu 2019 Comput. Mater. Sci. validated); uniaxial deformation fallback if Murnaghan fails (fit_converged=False only — B0_prime outside [4, 20] is a WARNING annotation, not a fallback trigger), paired with a slower-rate rate-sensitivity check; Born+NVT REMOVED (PCFF+PPPM virial incompatibility — K_Born 8-15x too high, Var(P) ~10^7x too high, failed 3/3 pipeline runs PMMA4/PVC1/PEEK1 2026-06-21; see BM_ANALYSIS.md)

rubbery bulk_modulus via Murnaghan EOS sweep at T>Tg; volume fluctuation is cross-check only. With no class-level bm_pressures_atm, Murnaghan now always submits (2026-08-09) via guides/MURNAGHAN.md's two-leg PROBE protocol (compression to 15000 atm + a shallow -200 atm tension probe; a clean probe earns a follow-up leg at the POXI-validated -1000 atm depth) instead of the old all-null/fluctuation-only skip -- a measured cohesive-energy-density signal was investigated as a per-system predictor for this but found directionally right, not precise enough to gate on, so the protocol is empirical (per-system probe outcome) rather than predictive

reportability is mechanized as bm_gate_verdict (Murnaghan) and deform_gate_verdict (deformation) — route on them, never re-derive. INADMISSIBLE blocks writing a K and halts to human review; FALLBACK_TO_DEFORM routes to the deformation path; r_squared>=0.999 and B0_prime outside [4,20] stay WARNINGS and never block. Deformation extraction MUST be passed deform_direction matching the deck's strain axis — a y/z leg analysed as x puts a loading slope into the transverse average, corrupting C11/C12/G/E/nu and isotropy_delta_pct and often flipping G and E negative (PLA2 deform_y: G -0.599 -> +1.105 GPa, isotropy 56.25% -> 4.62%). K is invariant, being one third of the response trace, so the historical 'G<0 is small-cell anisotropy' explanation was describing this bug, not physics

a family K is reportable only with >=3 replicates carrying a value, and no replicate flagged by aggregate_replicates.py's dispersion check (>4 leave-one-out SDs AND >10% from the other replicates' mean)
is_glassy from measured Tg>300K when tg requested, else from experimental_tg_K glassy_hint -- superseded for multi-member classes by the pinned-Tg clause below

for a multi-member class (experimental_tg_K is an OBJECT keyed by member name, e.g. PVNL {PVA:303,PVC:354,PVAc:304}; also PACR, POXI), the planner MUST resolve which member the SMILES is (by substituent — PVNL: *CC(Cl)*=PVC, *CC(O)*=PVA, *CC(OC(C)=O)*=PVAc) and pin THAT member's exp Tg/density/K in the D-04 evidence and assumptions[]. Drive is_glassy off the pinned exp Tg, never the noisy MD Tg — otherwise is_glassy/grading use the wrong target
property_method.rationale_bm_admissibility: Bulk-modulus reportability is mechanized as bm_gate_verdict (Murnaghan) and deform_gate_verdict (deformation fallback) — route on them, never re-derive. INADMISSIBLE covers what physics entails: K<=0, B0'<=0, volume_monotonic=false (dV/dP>0 violates mechanical stability — re-run the offending pressure point, do not re-fit), V0 outside the sampled volume range by >25% of its width (unsupported zero-pressure reference; the archive's worst legitimate extrapolation is 4.4%), r_squared<0.99 (Murnaghan form does not describe the data at all), and deform isotropy_delta_pct>=20%. That last one is NOT because K is ill-defined under anisotropy — K=(C11+2*C12)/3 is one third of the response trace and is invariant to which axis is labelled loading. It is because a SINGLE-direction Voigt K is a biased estimator when the cell is genuinely anisotropic: only one of three inequivalent directions was sampled. Evidence: PLA2's three legs give K 3.275/3.421/3.553 (8.1% spread) and its most anisotropic leg (deform_x, 28.1%) is also its worst K outlier, while PVC1's single anisotropic leg (24.2%) returns K=1.68 GPa against a Murnaghan 2.85 — 41% low. Shear-derived moduli are hit ~5x harder than K (PLA2 G spread 44.6% vs K 8.1%), so G/E/nu are the worst casualties, but K is affected enough to block. Zero of 36 archived runs violate any of these, which is the expected result for admissibility gates and no argument against them. r_squared>=0.999 is deliberately NOT binding: it has no power to predict B0 accuracy (mean |dB0| vs family mean 4.39% below 0.999 vs 4.37% at or above, Welch p=0.990; Spearman -0.066) and at that threshold rejects the two most accurate runs in the archive (PVC1 r2=0.99596 at 0.48% from its family mean, PEEK4 r2=0.99812 at 0.29%) while passing cis-PBD3 at 16.3% low. It stays a warning and the trim-selection criterion. Leave-one-out dB0 is emitted without a threshold: whole-replicate dispersion is 4.4% mean / 16.6% worst, so a >10% single-point shift is not yet shown to be pathological, and no archived or live run carries leave_one_out_refits to calibrate against.
property_method.rationale_replicate_dispersion: The only check that catches a run passing every per-run gate while disagreeing with its siblings — cis-PBD3's K is 16.3% below its family mean at r_squared=0.9985 with no admissibility violation. Measured in LEAVE-ONE-OUT SDs because a pooled-SD rule is unsatisfiable at small n: the largest deviation one point can have is (n-1)/sqrt(n) pooled SDs, i.e. 1.5 at n=4, so a 'beyond 2 SD' rule can never fire on a 4-replicate family — the outlier inflates the SD it is compared against. Excluding the candidate first gives cis-PBD3 16.0 LOO-SD against 2.1-3.4 for every other family's worst point. Requires BOTH >4 LOO-SD and >10% deviation: LOO-SD alone flags trivially small gaps when the remaining replicates agree tightly (PVC3, 2.7 LOO-SD on 3.0%), and a percentage alone flags ordinary scatter (PS4 15.3%, PLA3 13.7%). A property needs >=3 replicates with values to be reportable.
property_method.rationale: Born+NVT PCFF virial incompatibility confirmed 2026-06-21 across PMMA4, PVC1, PEEK1. Even a 4-ns run (PEEK1) gave K_T=-49.6 GPa. Wu (2019) Comput. Mater. Sci. validates NPT compression as faster and more reliable than volume-fluctuation for polymer K. Murnaghan reuses existing run_bulk_modulus_series tooling; glassy path uses npt_prod300_out.data at 300 K — with no bm_pressures_atm, guides/MURNAGHAN.md's fallback is the 5-point ladder [-1000,0,3000,7000,15000] atm (glassy single-leg, not rubbery PROBE, not symmetric ±1000).

stage_schema_requirements.description: Schema that every planned_stages entry must satisfy. The Critic enforces this in step 3 for reasoned plans; make_deterministic_plan.py satisfies it automatically via the STAGE_TRACK dict.

uncertainty_reduction_probes.description: Optional cheap experiments a reasoned plan may schedule BEFORE the full pipeline to reduce the dominant uncertainty. Each maps to an existing or planned ROADMAP capability.

fast_density_screen.mechanism: small-cell short NPT; compare density to experimental within +/-10%; max 2 FF retries (ROADMAP E3, currently BLOCKED on A1/A2 — record as planned, not executed, until unblocked).

literature_anchor.mechanism: search_ff_literature(smiles, name) -> reference FF + density/Tg targets + DOI (ROADMAP E2).

hardware_benchmark.reduces: hardware_optimum — the mpi/gpu config uncertainty for an off-table FF, an unusually sized cell, or a host whose hardware_policy is not cleanly benchmarked (values_are_benchmarked=false or host mismatch)
hardware_benchmark.mechanism: hardware/calibrate_hardware.py (wrapping hardware/benchmark_hardware.py) sweeps the mpi/gpu matrix on the built .data per template cost class, reports ns/day + Pair/Kspace/Neigh/Comm breakdown, names the winner, and writes directional_probe + by_forcefield (the latter only on a clean uncontended sweep). Runs politely around live runs (idle GPU + spare cores only, niced, sequential).
